grammar.karakaSummary: Sarvam idam is neuter subject of the first asti. In the Candrikā's explicit construction, ca has ced (‘if’) force: na anubhūtam is the condition and no kiṃcana kvacid ihāsti its consequence, with kiṃcana as subject under negation. Śāntam, sat, ekam, idam, and ānanam remain a difficult neuter chain with āste. Saṃtyaktaśaṅkam and apabhedam are adverbial state-accusatives with tvam āssva.
grammar.verbalModality: Asti occurs twice in the present; the second is conditionally scoped by ca in ced-artha according to the Candrikā. Āste is present third singular middle; āssva is second singular middle imperative. Bhūta, anubhūta, śānta, and saṃtyakta are participial formations.
